requirements.requirement: All existing content under /srv/inventory is owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: Final and post-restart recursive observations show every directory and file owned by inventorysvc, with explicit policy checks confirming no exceptions.

requirements.requirement: The inventory data is readable by inventory-readers.
requirements.summary: Directories have group read/traverse permissions, files have group read permission, and direct access tests using the inventory-readers GID successfully read and hash both files before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: The inventory data is inaccessible to other users.
requirements.summary: Every entry has zero other-user permission bits, and direct read attempts under an unrelated UID and GID were denied both before and after restart.
The same two files remain present, and their SHA-256 hashes exactly match the preparation baseline before repair, after repair, and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remained unchanged through completion and restart. The repair used successfully executing native account and permission tools without installing or replacing software.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state was captured, the restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and the running system, identities, permissions, hashes, and access behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the service identity and reader group was a necessary prerequisite, and changing ownership and modes directly implemented the requested access policy. The scheduled transient reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol and left no failed unit or unexpected persistent residue. Post-restart package health, failed-service state, and listening sockets remained healthy; PID and systemd-private-directory changes are normal reboot effects.
